title: Summer and Postcard
premise: Marine biologist Lior Halloran retreats to her family's struggling coastal vineyard after a public scandal destroyed her research career, counting sea turtles instead of facing the colleagues she believes betrayed her. When a freak snowstorm traps her with Theo Vance—the rival scientist who took credit for her work—and Mara, the ex-best friend who chose ambition over loyalty, three buried truths surface faster than the wine can breathe. As thaw comes and the vineyard's first harvest approaches, Lior must decide whether justice means exposure or something harder: forgiving herself for the choices that made her invisible. She ends not by destroying Theo publicly but by reclaiming her name on her own terms—and choosing love that doesn't require her to disappear.
about_author: Dominic Halloran is a former fisheries observer who traded deck logs for love stories set where the land meets cold water. He writes from a drafty farmhouse on the Atlantic coast, where his neighbors still suspect him of being a retired detective.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Three years after her career imploded, Lior logs turtle nests at her family vineyard's shoreline, hiding behind routine and her brother's failing winery. When a letter arrives announcing an industry conference at which Theo Vance will keynote, she almost burns it. Beat: numbness as armor.

chapters.title: The Vineyard Ledger
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The vineyard is drowning in debt; Lior agrees to host a small winter industry retreat for money, not knowing Theo organized it. Her brother Dev begs her to stay through it. Beat: dread disguised as pragmatism.

chapters.title: First Frost, First Face
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo arrives early, hoping to make amends before witnesses, and finds Lior knee-deep in a cold tank rescuing a stranded turtle. Their first exchange is barbed but electric—old intimacy under new hostility. Beat: recognition neither can deny.

chapters.title: Guests of the Storm
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The retreat guests arrive; among them is Mara Chen, Lior's former best friend who testified ambiguously during the scandal. Small talk curdles. The forecast turns vicious. Beat: the past seated at dinner.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The snowstorm knocks out power and roads; most guests evacuate ahead of it, stranding Lior, Theo, and Mara together with no cell service. The generator fails by midnight. Beat: forced proximity as pressure cooker.

chapters.title: Candlelight Confessions
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. By candlelight, Mara admits she saw Theo take Lior's data years ago and stayed silent because he promised her a career. Lior walks out into the snow rather than hear more. Beat: betrayal given a face and a reason.

chapters.title: What the Ice Keeps
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo follows Lior to the boathouse and confesses the full theft—not just data, but the grant proposal she drafted at twenty-six. He claims he was drowning too. She tells him confession isn't restitution. Beat: anger sharpened into clarity.

chapters.title: Morning After the Mistake
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Waking beside Theo after a night of grief-fueled closeness, Lior despises herself more than him. Mara watches them across the kitchen with unreadable eyes. Beat: shame as the true antagonist.

chapters.title: Thaw Lines
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Roads clear; guests trickle back for the retreat's final day. Theo quietly redirects a panel discussion to credit 'unattributed foundational research,' a half-gesture Lior notices and refuses to thank. Beat: insufficient penance.

chapters.title: The Mirror Room
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Alone, Lior rereads her old lab notebooks and confronts her own role: she signed away attribution to keep the peace, afraid of conflict, afraid of wanting too much. Beat: turning inward—the enemy in the mirror.

chapters.title: Mara's Bargain
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara offers Lior a deal: her testimony in exchange for co-authorship on Lior's dormant turtle-migration paper. Lior is disgusted by the transactional shape of justice—but tempted. Beat: ethics vs. survival.

chapters.title: Pruning Season
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Winter pruning in the vines with Dev, Lior admits she misses science itself, not the status. Dev reveals the vineyard will be sold unless harvest revenue doubles. Beat: stakes made concrete on two fronts.

chapters.title: Postcards, Unsigned
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo begins mailing Lior unsigned postcards—one per week, each quoting a line from her stolen proposal, each an installment of accountability. She never replies but keeps every one. Beat: courtship through contrition.

chapters.title: The Whistleblower's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A journalist contacts Lior about the scandal; going public could clear her name but torch Mara and derail the vineyard's fragile recovery. Lior drafts the email and deletes it four times. Beat: justice outside the law takes shape.

chapters.title: Harvest Hands
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Harvest begins; Theo shows up uninvited to work the crush pad for free. Grudging teamwork in the cellar softens something between them—until Mara arrives and sees them laughing. Beat: love against duty, first bloom.

chapters.title: Mara Breaks
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Feeling replaced twice over, Mara threatens to publish her own tell-all that would paint Lior as complicit in falsified field notes—a lie, but a plausible one. Beat: the rival weaponizes the truth's shadow.

chapters.title: Night Swim
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Overwhelmed, Lior swims the cold cove at night and nearly drowns; Theo pulls her out. On the rocks, shivering, she finally says aloud what she wants: her name restored, her work continued, him—if he's real. Beat: vulnerability as climax threshold.

chapters.title: The Hearing That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Instead of letting Lior fight alone, Theo submits a full confession to the funding agency and resigns his post, ending his career to begin hers again. Lior learns via the journalist's call. Beat: sacrifice without permission—love and fury collide.

chapters.title: What We Owe Each Other
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Furious that he acted without her consent, Lior confronts Theo: she didn't need saving, she needed partnership. He listens—for once—and asks what she actually wants. She asks for time. Beat: power rebalanced.

chapters.title: Mara's Testimony
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara withdraws her threat and instead gives the journalist a sworn account corroborating Lior's authorship, accepting her own disgrace. The two women meet at the shoreline tanks; forgiveness is offered, not yet accepted. Beat: justice completed by the wounded witness.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The vineyard's first bottles are labeled; the turtle hatchlings emerge at dawn and Lior, now reinstated to lead a coastal research station, releases them with Dev and the cellar crew. Theo waits at the edge, invited but uncertain. Beat: reclamation.

chapters.title: Summer, Signed
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Weeks later, Lior mails Theo a single postcard—her handwriting, her name, a date and a tide chart. He arrives at the cove at the appointed hour. They begin again as equals, on the record. Beat: love chosen openly, invisibility ended.
